solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Satisfied, read news out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone content after reading the news aloud to others.
explanation.definitionFit: To have answered a demand or need is to have satisfied it.

clue.text: Welsh town hospital after orderly

indicators.note: after places the hospital letter behind the word for orderly

parts.note: orderly means neat and tidy

explanation.surface: Directions to a Welsh town's hospital, found just past a hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital worker beside 'hospital', but it is the adjective meaning tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a town in south Wales, near Swansea.

clue.text: Union band?

parts.note: the union is a marriage and the band is the circle of metal worn on the finger, not a trade union or a musical group

explanation.definitionFit: The ring exchanged at a wedding is the band that symbolises the marital union.

clue.text: One may get a story about hospital worker

parts.note: re is Latin-derived crossword shorthand for about or concerning
a porter moves patients and equipment around a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital worker might be a source of gossip for someone chasing a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist's job is to obtain stories and write them up.

clue.text: Biblical combatants who stood within a stone's throw of each other?

definitions.text: Biblical combatants who stood within a stone's throw of each other?

parts.words: Biblical combatants who stood within a stone's throw of each other?
parts.note: the idiom for being close by is taken literally, since the shepherd boy felled the giant with a stone from his sling

explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Samuel the young shepherd kills the Philistine giant with a slingshot stone.

clue.text: Bloodhound in film

definitions.meaning: a bloodhound, figuratively, is a dogged detective who tracks people down
a 1972 thriller starring Laurence Olivier and Michael Caine, remade in 2007

explanation.surface: A tracking dog appearing in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share a name: the figurative tracker is a detective, and the Olivier–Caine thriller bears that title.

clue.text: Unctuous substance placed on right tray

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a salve is a greasy healing ointment

explanation.surface: Some ointment set down on the right-hand tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A salver is a flat serving tray, often silver, used for drinks or cards.

clue.text: Age of English artist

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: How old a particular English painter is.
explanation.definitionFit: An age and an era are both long periods of history.

clue.text: Film director, heading for town, relaxed on a train

indicators.note: heading means the front letter, the one at the head of the word town
relaxed means loosened from its order, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A movie director on the way to town, unwinding on a rail journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is the director of Pulp Fiction and Reservoir Dogs.

clue.text: Difficult to get ahead, being short of money

parts.note: hard means difficult
up means ahead, as in being a goal up

explanation.surface: Finding it tough to make progress when one is broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard up is the idiom for lacking cash.

clue.text: Satirist displaying anger after dance

indicators.note: after puts the anger word behind the dance in the answer

parts.note: the volta is a lively Renaissance dance for couples
ire means anger

explanation.surface: A satirical writer showing fury once the dancing is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Enlightenment writer of Candide was a celebrated satirist.

clue.text: Asian sea bream husband caught

indicators.note: caught means held inside, so the husband letter is trapped within the fish

parts.note: tai is a Japanese name for sea bream, familiar from crosswords

explanation.surface: A husband landing a sea bream somewhere in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand is described by this nationality word, an Asian people.

clue.text: Misleading clue embarrassed Holmes, initially slipping up

parts.note: red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the detective's name is taken

parts.note: erring means making a mistake, slipping up

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes red-faced after a false lead made him blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A false lead planted to distract investigators is the classic misleading clue.

clue.text: Wave bowler hat in US skating race

parts.note: a roller is a long heavy wave breaking on the shore
derby is the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.surface: Someone waving a bowler hat at an American skating contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contact sport on roller skates, raced round an oval track, largely American in origin.

clue.text: Permit to get inside enclosure is a specific colour

indicators.note: says the permit word goes within the enclosure word

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
to agree to something is to permit it

explanation.surface: A licence is needed to enter a fenced area of a particular hue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright yellowish green named after the colour of fresh garden peas.

clue.text: Leader one's spoken about after tide turned

indicators.note: after puts the spoken piece behind the turned tide
turned means the word tide is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

indicators.note: about means the spoken word goes round the letter for one

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A leader's speech remarked on once the tide had changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article is its leader, giving the paper's own opinion.

clue.text: Hideaway left warm and dry

parts.note: to air laundry is to warm and dry it, as in an airing cupboard

explanation.surface: A refuge abandoned, though it stayed cosy and dry.
explanation.walkthrough: To air clothes is a British usage: hanging them in a warm airing cupboard to finish drying.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a wild animal's den, and loosely any hiding place.

clue.text: Plants grow wild in spasms

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the word for spasms

parts.note: fits are sudden spasms or seizures

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of grow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Vegetation sprouting uncontrollably in sudden bursts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' makes GWOR; 'spasms' reads like a verb in the surface but is the plural noun for sudden attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Figworts are a genus of herbaceous flowering plants, Scrophularia.

clue.text: Flightless bird from West Indies seen on jetty, reportedly

indicators.note: seen on puts the West Indies letters after the jetty piece in this across entry
reportedly says the word for jetty is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a quay is a landing place or jetty

explanation.surface: A bird that cannot fly, imported from the Caribbean and spotted at the docks.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is New Zealand's national bird and cannot fly.

clue.text: Girl Scout, to do good, provides a help for one who's blind

definitions.text: a help for one who's blind

parts.note: a Guide is a member of the Girl Guides, the British equivalent of Girl Scouts
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Girl Scout's good deed is assisting a blind person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to do good' reads as the Scout's motto-like aim, but splits into DO and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A trained dog leads a visually impaired owner safely through the streets.

clue.text: Become furious in diocese over cardinal?

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece is written above the second

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese
cardinal red is the scarlet of a cardinal's robes

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper in a diocese about a senior churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a church dignitary, but here it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is the idiom for suddenly getting very angry.

clue.text: Poet, verbose member of a learned society

parts.note: long-winded, so long means verbose
a fellow is a member of a learned body such as the Royal Society

explanation.surface: A poet who is a wordy academician.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was the American poet of Hiawatha.

clue.text: Record some of Verdi's compositions

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recording of a selection of Verdi's operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or CD.

clue.text: American brought over his cracked Japanese dish

indicators.note: in a down entry the American piece is placed above the rest
cracked means broken up, so the letters of his are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American carried his broken Japanese plate across.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Drink, Italian, brought back by a girl

indicators.note: by means set next to the following pieces
brought back means the abbreviation for Italian is read in reverse

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An Italian brings home a drink with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tia Maria is a coffee liqueur.

clue.text: Damage sign, knocking end off

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for sign is removed

parts.note: a mark is a sign or symbol

explanation.surface: Vandalising a sign by breaking its end off.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it.

clue.text: Most uncommon seeing rats scurrying round about

indicators.note: round means the scrambled rats go around the word for about
rats scurrying run every which way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An unusual sight: rodents dashing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scurrying' makes RAST; 'seeing' is just a link joining the definition to the wordplay, not a sight in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarest is the superlative of rare, meaning least common.

clue.text: Using unusual words in US state, briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the state's last letter is dropped

parts.note: Florida is a US state

explanation.surface: Speaking with exotic vocabulary while in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Florid prose is ornate and flowery, full of elaborate expressions.

clue.text: Is shy, after misbehaving with proper tantrum

indicators.note: misbehaving letters are out of order, so is shy is rearranged

parts.note: fit means proper or suitable

explanation.surface: A shy child who turns naughty and throws a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A hissy fit is a petulant outburst, an informal word for a tantrum.
